page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.56-896 is a high-capacity flexible virtual machine instance powered by third-generation Intel Xeon 8358 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture with a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz, the configuration supplies 56 dedicated physical cores and 112 virtual processing units with symmetric multithreading enabled at two threads per core. System memory totals 896.0 GB of RAM, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance contains no integrated local storage and relies on network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data management. It also contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs, focusing all provisioned resources on CPU and memory throughput. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Regarding cost efficiency, the high resource density paired with an eight-to-one memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-effective platform for memory-demanding workloads without the expense associated with specialized hardware accelerators.

Given the 112-vCPU processing capacity and 896.0 GB memory footprint, VM.Standard3.Flex.56-896 is structured for large in-memory databases, distributed caching, extract-transform-load batch processing, big data analytics engines, and high-concurrency enterprise backend applications.
